title: libpod: don't run rootless containers without a cgroup when cgroups are enabled
body:
In rootless cgroupfs mode without `--cgroup-parent`, Podman leaves the OCI cgroup path empty. When the runtime then fails to create a cgroup, crun and runc run the container
 without one. With `--pid=host` that leaves a container that `podman stop` can't stop (see #XXXX).

   Podman now creates the cgroup itself before calling the runtime. It tries `/libpod-<id>` first, then `libpod-<id>` next to its own cgroup, and writes the one that worked into the
 OCI spec. If neither works, the container fails to start. The cgroup is removed again if container creation fails before the runtime takes over. Explicit `--cgroup-parent`, systemd
 and rootful are unchanged.

   This also allows `--cgroups=disabled --pid=host` for runtimes in both `runtime_supports_kvm` and `runtime_supports_nocgroup` (krun by default). Their workload runs in a VM, so the
 private PID namespace requirement doesn't buy anything there. Joining another container's PID namespace is still rejected, and `--cgroups=enabled` still fails instead of falling
 back. To check the runtime capabilities, the runtime is now resolved before `validate()`.

   Depends on: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1307

   I didn't touch go.mod or vendor; I'll vendor container-libs once that PR is merged, so this won't build until then. Opening as draft.

   Tested with new system tests in `420-cgroups.bats` and unit tests for the PID namespace validation. I also ran crun and runc manually with a read-only cgroup view and with only
 the sibling location writable, and krun with `--cgroups=disabled --pid=host`, against a build with the container-libs change vendored.

   Fixes: #30078

comments.body: [NON-BLOCKING] Packit jobs failed. @podman-container-tools/packit-jobs please check. Everyone else, feel free to ignore.

The Packit failures are expected for now. This PR uses `cgroups.CreateFirst` from https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1307, which isn't vendored yet, so
 the build fails with `undefined: cgroups.CreateFirst`.

   I left go.mod and vendor untouched on purpose and will vendor container-libs once https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/1307 is merged. Until then I'll keep this as a draft.

   I tested it locally with the container-libs change vendored: unit tests, the new tests in 420-cgroups.bats, and golangci-lint. Feedback on the approach is welcome in the meantime.

this is wrong, on cgroup v2, you can't create cgroups under the current one (that already holds the Podman process) and move processes there.

Creating the cgroup must be owned by the OCI runtime.

I'll close both PRs because I don't think this is the correct thing to do
